verdict.tagline: Dive back into the depths, though the waters are still choppy.
for_you_if: you want to explore alien oceans with friends
you enjoy base building in underwater environments
not_for_you_if: you expect lethal combat options against hostile wildlife
you are waiting for a complete story right now
you need stable frame rates without performance issues
you want frequent content updates during early access

cohorts.summary: Early players encounter content limits, slow updates, and technical instability alongside design choices that restrict combat options.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the map feels too small and limited in its current early access state.

citations.review_text: The exploration and mechanics are really good, and I've been enjoying them a lot. My only real complaint is that the map feels a little too small in my opinion. However, considering the game is still in development, it's understandable, and I'm looking forward to seeing how much bigger and better it gets. Very fun game overall.

Overall, the game is really great! The sound design, graphics, animations, and overall atmosphere are amazing. I'm really looking forward to the full release of *Subnautica 2*. I've already completed the storyline available in Early Access, and I can't wait for future updates that will expand the world and give us more things to explore, since the current playable area is still quite limited.

The multiplayer experience is also really fun, especially when playing with friends. However, I feel like the game is still missing some hostile creatures and terrifying encounters, similar to the jumpscares and dangerous creatures from the first *Subnautica*. I really want to experience that same fear and tension while exploring with a friend, and I think adding more dangerous creatures to *Subnautica 2* would make the experience even better.

For now, I think the game still lacks a bit of action and horror. While exploring, I don't really feel that same sense of fear or urgency that made the first game so memorable. I want those moments where something suddenly appears, where I have to swim for my life, or where exploring the depths genuinely makes me feel terrified. Overall, the game has a lot of potential, and I'm excited to see how much more intense, immersive, and frightening it becomes in future updates.
i loved the game the only thing i don't like is how small the map feels i like games with many different biomes and animals but the game is not done so only time can tell the future

claims.claim: Reviewers complain about a lack of content updates and slow development progress during early access.

citations.review_text: Big fan of the people screaming its in early access like that should mean that a game that made more than 5 mill in sales is this damn slow updating.

DO NOT BUY

Barely any content and no updates for 6+ months. Pathetic devlogs are all thats there to make it seem like theres work being done.

Consider it dead for now, maybe forever.

I bought this game fully aware that it wasn't finished and was in early access. 6 months later there hasn't been a single content update. Every few weeks theres a new dev log in their discord and they keep promising the new update. It has been 6 months, I spent 30 USD on launch. Its sad because I love subnautica and probably have 200 hours in both the original and below zero. 

Don't spend your money until the game is fully released because you will feel scammed.

I think this game has a long way to go. 
Updates are coming out too slow.
The deep water sure looks scary.
But your wallet is what should be wary.
I really didn't expect this game to blow.

claims.claim: Reviewers state that players are unable to kill hostile alien fish or wildlife, limiting defensive options to avoidance and specific non-lethal tools.

citations.review_text: Game is fun and i can't wait for more areas to explore but the worst thing about this game is the stupid brain dead decision to remove killing the alien fish. Like really give me a knife, speargun, and so forth. The game talks about dying and mass death but oh we can't kill the fish that are killing us???? seriously make that make sense!! I hope someone creates a mod that adds the feature the devs are too stupid to implement themselves.. Review will change once the game changes.

Disappointing game. There is no proper combat system. Instead of fighting enemies, you spend most of your time hiding and running away. You can't even kill wild animals, which makes the experience even more frustrating. This is not what I expected from this game.

I'll check back sometime in the future to see if things have improved. If the developers make meaningful changes and fix these issues, I'll gladly update my review.

claims.claim: Reviewers mention that respawning after death removes the sense of danger, urgency, and consequences for the player character.

citations.review_text: This game is absolutely worth it, the modding community is growing and will probably out-shadow the subnautica one mods, this game will also likely have more vehicles than subnautica 1. This is game is great for multiplayer or even single player. I absolutely recommend this game. I will say though, the fact that we are reprinted removes the feeling of urgency of getting out of harm's way, it removes all feeling of danger and it detaches you from your character because if you die you can just reprint with little to none consequences. I whole-heartedly believe that this game will improve and (hopefully) fix this issue, unfortunately this problem, quite frankly, sucks.

While the bones of a good game are here, it's nothing like the original game. 
  The animation is beautiful, and the different biomes are interesting, but the clone aspect of the story makes everything fall flat.
  There is no threat of death. Urgency only comes in moments of sudden shock at new things, which would be diluted on any future playthrough.
   I can only hold onto hope that the story will be completely changed, and that the bland clone situation is done away with entirely.

 In it's current state, this game is not worth playing or buying yet.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the game features a cooperative multiplayer mode which allows playing with friends.

citations.review_text: Love this game, while It dose take a while for updates to come out I understand as the team is working hard and I rather have high quality updates. Exploring is fun yet dreadfull as you dont know whats around the corner. I do wish there was more methods of defense however, if we cant kill at least let us defend are selfs better. That and scanning the lethithans is a absolute pain even with biomods like the invisibly. The soundtrack is good and so are the environmental designs and Fish. I'm also glad that I can finally play with friend's. I do hope for more base modifcations and design options as I love building and decorating.
Conquer a new planet and new fish.. but with friends!! 10/10

A true sequel to an already perfect game.

Game runs pretty well on my oldish hardware. The co-op really adds a lot of spice that the original simply didn't have. The visuals and and soundtrack are amazing, and I'd say they stand up to, or are even better than the first game and it's standalone DLC Below Zero.

Of course at the time of writing this review, the game is still in Early Access, and not all features are available. Just seeing what they have so far, however, is really impressive. I can't wait to see how they continue to reinvent the wheel with this one.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the game includes base building mechanics and customization options.

citations.review_text: Love this game, while It dose take a while for updates to come out I understand as the team is working hard and I rather have high quality updates. Exploring is fun yet dreadfull as you dont know whats around the corner. I do wish there was more methods of defense however, if we cant kill at least let us defend are selfs better. That and scanning the lethithans is a absolute pain even with biomods like the invisibly. The soundtrack is good and so are the environmental designs and Fish. I'm also glad that I can finally play with friend's. I do hope for more base modifcations and design options as I love building and decorating.

I would not recommend purchasing the game as is in early access. I do generally enjoy the game, though it is not without its faults. If you have somehow stumbled across this review and have not played the first Subnautica game, do. I'd recommend that much more than this game in its current state. The contents of this review are free from spoilers, though my commentary is limited.

[h1]Cons:[/h1]

[h2]Performance[/h2]
People who ran the first game may not be able to run this game.

[h2]TAA[/h2]
The game has noticeable ghosting in many places, and quality of the picture in motion is generally poor. There is no option to use a different method of anti-aliasing, or to disable it altogether.

[h2]Music[/h2]
The soundtrack is unfortunately poor compared to subnautica's original, unfortunately. I am not fond of the music that plays when one of the creatures is after you.

[h2]It's Early Access[/h2]
Bugs, incomplete storyline, et cetera. This is the main reason I can't outright recommend it.

[h1]Pros:[/h1]

[h2]Better Bases[/h2]
I generally prefer the way bases are constructed in this game compared to the first one.

[h2]Compelling Story[/h2]
The story and lore are very compelling. The voice actors and writers all did outstanding work.

[h2]Environment[/h2]
The ocean feels very tight-knit and there are interesting tidbits of speculative evolution in it. I quite enjoy it.

[h2]Structures[/h2]
All of the structures found on the planet are awe-inspiring and fun to explore. They are stylistically amazing.

[h2]Vehicles[/h2]
8/10 currently, no notes. Waiting for the cyclops analog to be filled before I can say more.

[h2]New Game Mechanics[/h2]
Limiting myself in the interest of potential spoilers, I think generally that the new game mechanics work well.

i cant kill the fish. they went from a great crafting survival game with defensive mechanics, to the absolute most butt bare minimum "avoid the monster" trope game. 50% of the reason i even bought subnautica 1 was because i could interact with the environment. if i cant kill a young peeper and make its parents watch then this game is useless. its literally just a "walk forward, get thing, hope you dont die to a monster, walk back, craft, repeat" with absolutely no defensive mechanics. this game is basically every way that subnautica 1 failed but with almost nothing that it triumphed, except a slightly better base building. its barely even a sandbox game

this is one of the best games i have ever played, this franchise is one of the best i have ever played. what i would like to see added 1. be able to kill things like subnatca 1 with the fart bombs and stasis rifle or kill leviathans in other ways plus be able to kill things with the multitool. 2. have the biome with tongue thief's useful i used the biome once for trolleite.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe performance issues, lag in multiplayer, or frame rate instability requiring players to limit their FPS.

citations.review_text: Its Good but a bit laggy in multiplayer
Amazing game, basically subnautica 1 but better. If your computer shuts of randomly during play time, limit your FPS to 30 with the in game settings
its good but if you dont have good computer it will be super laggy i think they should add a mode so that its less laggy, subnautica please see this

So far it is an amazing continuation of the first game.
It looks beautiful. Lots of quality of life improvements. Base building is flexible. Even now there is a good amount of areas to explore in early access. The performance is a work in progress, I guess. But by now I have managed to get a stable frame rate on medium to epic settings.
As somebody with thalassophobia the ocean feels more terrifying. Distant blur, ups and downs of the surface causing more sections where it feels there is abyss down below.
Will not spoil leviathans. But one looks intimidating and deadly. One is random and sudden. And one is by now, to me, a nightmare fuel. I would agree with other people who say that music slightly ruins the "surprise" but during the danger - it amplifies the fear. I really hope if we get large submarine - it won't save us like how it is with the Reaper leviathan.
Additionally, whoever on team made one certain biomod that helps hide from a predator's sight - I both hate and love you. It is genius and cruel torture on somebody with the phobia, like myself. I had an episode where it worked flawlessly to drain my entire soul.

I wish Unknown Worlds Entertainment good workflow and, importantly, patience with the development. I believe in you all.
